claims.text: ADR 0027 header: not built at stage-4; Notifications still sends only email as at stage-3.

Stage-3/4 SendOneAsync order: SendAsync first, then Status = "sent" and SentAt; the round is saved later in CompleteAsync. A crash after sending and before the save leaves the row pending, so it is sent again. On a stop the catch's when filter skips RecordFailure.
A failed SendAsync call goes to RecordFailure, which keeps the row pending with a later NextAttemptAt (another attempt); the fifth failure (MaxAttempts = 5) marks the row failed.

ADR 0027 decision: email at-least-once, always sent for every order message, the main channel; SMS and push at-most-once: the row is marked before the provider call, and an error unclear whether sent is not retried.
Review drivers, ranked: 1 no order email lost; 2 email within minutes (assumed); 3 one shop's busy day not slowing others; 4 a paid SMS not sent twice.
ADR 0027 consequence: losing an SMS when Notifications stops mid-way is acceptable only because the same message always has an email; dropping email from a kind of message means reviewing the ADR.
Review: sensitivity point: email is the main channel; the SMS choice is safe only while every order message also goes by email; dropping email from a kind of message reopens ADR 0027.

Review trade-off points: email at-least-once (helps driver 1, may arrive twice); SMS and push at-most-once (helps driver 4, may lose one); pacing trades delay for not being refused (hurts driver 2 after an outage, helps driver 1).
Rejected options in the review: one loop for every channel; API or each service calling providers (against ADR 0002); SMS at-least-once (against driver 4).

Review bottleneck: the provider's allowed rate, not the sender; more than two copies of Notifications do not send faster. Two copies share 10 emails a second; one copy's ceiling is 10 rows per 2 s, 5 a second.
Review estimate (assumed): about 6.6 emails a second at the busiest hour, about 1.2 a second on an average day; Service A allows 10 emails a second (assumed, awaiting contract).

Review backlog (Little's law): one-hour outage at the busiest hour leaves about 6.6 x 3,600 = about 24,000 emails; drains at 10 - 6.6 = 3.4/s, about 2 hours; normal day about 4,300 emails, 8.8/s, about 8 minutes.

Two of ADR 0027's three review conditions (the provider idempotency-key one left out per depth_notes): a kind of message needs SMS without email; 24 hours of retries not enough for an outage of the email service.
ADR 0027 feedback received: a tester asked about customers choosing only SMS without email; answer: not allowed, email is always sent because that makes SMS at-most-once safe; product owner agreed.
Review risks table: the email service's allowed rate is an assumption; the product owner asks the provider before connecting Service A.

ADR 0027: pacing exists so the post-outage backlog is sent without refusals (design premise that sends above the rate are refused). Review: retries for 24 h (assumed), gap growing to a cap; after 24 h a row becomes failed, shown to operations to resend by hand.

claims.text: No order of send and save across a sender and an external provider gives exactly once delivery; each order chooses between a possible duplicate and a possible loss.
Opinion with condition: for order emails a missing email harms the customer more than a duplicate; where a duplicate does harm (e.g. a single-use code), the email row is weighed differently.

claims.text: Unpaced sending after an outage gets refusals; refused rows wait for another attempt with a growing gap and rows are claimed by next_attempt_at, so some emails can arrive later than ones queued after them.
